'''Caldo galego''' or simply ''caldo'' (in [[Galician language|Galician]]), also known as ''caldo gallego'' (in [[Spanish language|Spanish]]), meaning literally "Galician broth", is a traditional soup dish from [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cooks.com/rec/search/0,1-0,caldo_gallego,FF.html|title=Caldo Gallego - Recipes |website=Cooks.com|accessdate=2 October 2018}}</ref> It is essentially a regional derivative (with added beans and turnip greens) of the very similar ''[[caldo verde]]'', the traditional soup dish of neighbouring [[Portugal]].

Ingredients include ''repolo'' ([[cabbage]]), ''verzas'' ([[collard greens]]), ''[[Rapini|grelos]]'' (rapini), or ''navizas'' (sweet [[turnip]] greens); potatoes; [[white bean]]s; and ''unto'' (lard). Additionally it can contain fatty pork, ''[[chorizo]]'', ham, or bacon (''compango'').

It is served hot as a starter, often as part of ''almuerzo'' (lunch), and sometimes dinner. Traditionally it was usually served in ''cuncas'' (earthen bowls).
